problem: The sign discussion is truncated: 'opposite signs (Δ  0)' and 'or decay (τ < 0)' leave out the cases Δ < 0 and τ > 0, so the stability rule cannot be read correctly.
fix: Write: 'The sign of Δ says whether the eigenvalues have the same sign (Δ > 0) or opposite signs (Δ < 0). The sign of τ says whether they grow (τ > 0) or decay (τ < 0).'

problem: The condition is incomplete: 'Δ > 0, τ²  0' is missing '< 4Δ' and 'τ > 0'. As printed it does not define an unstable spiral.
fix: Change to 'Δ > 0, τ² < 4Δ, τ > 0 | complex, Re λ > 0 | unstable spiral | unstable'.

problem: It says eigenvectors give two special directions and a node has two stable/unstable directions. For a repeated real eigenvalue, there may be only one independent eigenvector, so this is false for an improper node.
fix: Qualify: 'For distinct real eigenvalues, eigenvectors give two directions. A saddle has one stable and one unstable direction; a node has two (or, in the repeated defective case, only one) stable/unstable eigendirections.'

problem: The answer adds '(improper node)', but equal eigenvalues do not force an improper node. If the repeated eigenvalue has two independent eigenvectors, it is a proper/star node; only the defective case is improper.
fix: Answer 'stable node, asymptotically stable'; add that proper versus improper depends on whether the eigenspace is two-dimensional or one-dimensional.

problem: The table omits the repeated-real-eigenvalue case τ² = 4Δ with Δ > 0. It jumps from τ² > 4Δ to τ² < 4Δ, so students cannot classify Q6 from the table.
fix: Add rows: 'Δ > 0, τ² = 4Δ, τ < 0 | real repeated | stable node | asymptotically stable' and 'Δ > 0, τ² = 4Δ, τ > 0 | real repeated | unstable node | unstable' (or note proper/improper depends on eigenvectors).
